name: SIS Ltd
title: SIS Ltd - 540673 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Record FY26 revenue and margin in security and FM, but the call offers no capacity, utilisation or pricing-discipline data; wage-driven pass-through and Labour Code tailwinds are the main supply-side story.

triggers.label: State minimum wage hikes 15-50%
triggers.quote: Haryana has hiked minimum wages by 50%, Uttar Pradesh by close to 28%

triggers.label: Labour Codes may curb non-compliant rivals
triggers.quote: the noncompliance trend in this sector, which has kept this industry rather fragmented

triggers.label: DSO down 4 days to 63
triggers.quote: one of the best DSO days, which is 63 days, down by 4 days from the previous quarter

guidance.quote: we want to continue doing what we are doing with a 15% return profile
Your EBITDA margins will hover around 5%, 6%, maybe 6.5%.
over the next 18 months odd, as we consolidate branches

red_flags.label: Rs290cr gratuity charge; Rs38.8cr reversed through OCI, past-period recovery unconfirmed
red_flags.quote: we are in discussion with our customers

red_flags.label: ECL provision up sharply to Rs50cr+
red_flags.quote: It's simply our Audit Committee pressing for being more prudent.

red_flags.label: Cash-business IPO deferred
red_flags.quote: the cash IPO is not delayed by us. It is deferred owing to circumstances

evasions.quote: We don't do guidance by segment even on a consol basis
I wouldn't be able to comment on that.
Well, it is a misquote, but it is also possible.

summary.headline: SIS Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 31% YoY to INR4,489 crore with a record INR207 crore EBITDA at 4.6% margin.
summary.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as its best quarter ever, with record revenue, EBITDA and PAT, and ROCE of 16.5% versus 14.3% a year earlier. India Security delivered its highest-ever revenue (INR1,925 crore, up 34.2%), partly from the APS acquisition, and International Security also posted record revenue (INR1,950 crore, up 36.9%). Facility Management was the slowest grower at 8.1% YoY to INR635 crore. A INR290 crore gratuity/leave charge taken in Q3 under the new Labour Codes was partly reversed (INR38.8 crore) through OCI in Q4, and management said past-period recovery from clients is under discussion.

financial_highlights.change: reassessment after Q3 INR290 crore exceptional charge

financial_highlights.value: INR70 crore in Q4 vs INR55 crore in Q3
financial_highlights.change: FY26 INR215 crore vs FY25 INR163 crore
up from about INR20 crore YoY

segments.name: India Security
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,925 crore (+34.2% YoY, includes APS consolidation); EBITDA INR98.4 crore at 5.1% margin. Ex-APS, Security grew 11% YoY at about 5.5% margin.

segments.name: Facility Management
segments.commentary: Revenue INR635 crore (+8.1% YoY); EBITDA margin 5.5%, up from roughly 4.5% previously. Management said the monthly run rate rose to INR31 crore versus INR21 crore a year ago. Headcount fell from about 85,000 to 82,000, which management attributed to closed contracts after surge work.

segments.name: International Security
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,950 crore (+36.9% YoY); EBITDA margin 3.8%, stable QoQ, with EBITDA up 28.7% YoY. Q4 included about AUD20 million from the Australian Open and Australian Grand Prix, which management said recur every Q4.

segments.name: APS (AP Securitas)
segments.commentary: Q4 EBITDA margin 4.2%, against 5% per one answer and 5.5% for SIS Security ex-APS; management targets closing the 50 bps gap over 18 months or more.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for 15%+ growth and 15%+ ROCE/ROE on a multi-year basis; it gave no segment-level guidance.
EBITDA margins are expected to hover around 5-6.5%; management declined to say whether 6% is reachable in FY27 or FY28.
APS margin gap closure to SIS levels is targeted over roughly 1-1.5 years via branch consolidation, back-office sharing and procurement integration.
Cash business (Q-Comm-type cash logistics) IPO is deferred; management hopes to proceed within FY27, with SEBI extending DRHP validity to September 30.
Management said a Rs 20,000 crore revenue figure attributed to it in the press was a misquote, though possible.
Labour Code wage pass-through is built into contracts; working-capital benefits from invoicing and collection changes are possible but unquantified.
capex_capacity: Depreciation rose INR15 crore QoQ, of which INR10 crore relates to a new Australian office lease (MSS lease), implying about INR40 crore annually.
25 residential training facilities across 14 states; supply centres in eastern, East India and Central India states.
Management cited depreciation averaging about 1.2% of revenue since FY21.
demand_pricing: Management said Labour Codes and minimum-wage hikes are a positive: Haryana raised minimum wages by about 50%, UP by about 28% (later referred to as about 20%), and Punjab and Uttarakhand by over 15% in the last 30 days.
SIS prices a few percentage points above local competitors, attributed to service fees, technology, training and kit fees.
Management said SIS holds about 5% security market share; the largest security firms in the US and UK hold more than 15%.
Management said SIS is about twice the size of Group 4, the next-largest Indian security company.
Corporate offices make up less than 10% of FM customers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FM margin sustainable and what is the monthly run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Rituraj Sinha said FM margins have moved from 4.5% or lower to about 5.5% and are sustainable. Monthly run rate was cited at INR31 crore versus INR21 crore a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: How long are International contracts and what was the Q4 bump?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikram Kannoth said Australia and New Zealand contracts run 3-5 years. Q4 events (Australian Open and Grand Prix) added about AUD20 million (about INR120 crore) without matching headcount, and Q1 normalises.

qa_highlights.question: What is the APS integration plan and margin gap?
qa_highlights.answer: APS Q4 margin was corrected to 4.2% against SIS Security's 5.5%. Management expects the gap to close over 1-1.5 years via branch consolidation, back-office sharing and procurement.

qa_highlights.question: Was the INR290 crore labour code charge reversal recognised in the P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: Brajesh Kumar said the INR38.8 crore reassessment must go through OCI under accounting norms. Future costs are passed through in customer rate cards; past-period amounts will be recovered when paid to retiring employees.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROE aspiration and how is the cash business IPO progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has no formal ROE target, but aims for 15%+ growth and returns above 15%, and wants PAT of INR500 crore to enter the top 100 listed companies. The cash IPO is deferred due to geopolitics and IPO market conditions; the company hopes to proceed in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation and expected credit loss rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation rose INR15 crore QoQ, of which INR10 crore was the Australian lease. Credit loss allowance rose to about INR50 crore from about INR20 crore YoY, which management called prudent provisioning requested by the Audit Committee.

risks_watch: Gratuity/leave liability: INR290 crore charge taken in Q3; recovery of past-period costs from clients is still under discussion and not accrued.
International revenue depends on Q4 event timing (Australian Open, Grand Prix); management says Q1 normalises.
APS margin at 4.2% against a target of about 5.5%; integration timing is 1-1.5 years or more.
Expected credit loss allowance rose to about INR50 crore from about INR20 crore YoY; management attributed this to prudence.
Minimum-wage hikes across several states could raise costs before pass-through, and labour unrest was reported in Haryana and Greater Noida.
Cash business IPO timing depends on geopolitics and market conditions; no fixed date.
FM headcount declined from about 85,000 to 82,000 and FM revenue growth was 8.1%.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY26 and Labour Code tailwinds, but cautious on the cash IPO timing and evasive on FY27 segment growth and when margins reach 6%. Management pushed back firmly on questions about one-offs and depreciation.
key_quotes: This industry is not a 10% EBITDA margin industry. This is a growth and ROCE industry.
The barriers are not to entry, the barriers are to scale.
So FY26 is a good story.

adds.what: Australian office lease (MSS lease) adding depreciation, not productive capacity
25 residential training facilities across 14 states (existing, no new additions stated)

growth.why: Management reiterated around 15% multi-year revenue CAGR and 15%+ ROCE, with EBITDA margins guided at 5-6.5%, but gave no segment guidance and no specific capacity, order or contract numbers behind the growth target, so backing is vague.
